subject: physics_2
question_text: What will be the ratio of the radii of two nuclei of mass numbers A₁ and A₂?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: R = R₀A^(1/3) with R₀ ≈ 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, so R₁/R₂ = (A₁/A₂)^(1/3). Written here with the cube-root sign ∛ because the exponent 1/3 has no honest one-line superscript form in Unicode. A worked check: A₁ = 27, A₂ = 8 gives R₁/R₂ = 3/2.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The radius relation
lines: The radius of a nucleus of mass number A is
where R₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m is a constant, the
steps.margin_note: First mark. State R = R₀∛A and say what R₀ is.
steps.why: Volume is proportional to R³, and a nucleus of mass number A holds A nucleons packed at one fixed density, so R³ ∝ A. Taking the cube root of both sides gives R ∝ ∛A.
common_mistakes: Writing R = R₀A. The dependence is on the cube root of A, not on A.
Forgetting to say that R₀ is the same constant for all nuclei.

recall.must_convey: That the nuclear radius is R = R₀ times the cube root of A, with R₀ a constant about 1.2 fermi.
accept: R equals R nought A to the power one third
R nought times cube root of A
radius goes as cube root of mass number
reject: ratio is A one by A two

steps.memory_tip: Same density everywhere, so volume ∝ A and radius ∝ ∛A.

steps.label: The ratio
lines: For two nuclei of mass numbers A₁ and A₂,
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Show R₀ cancelling, then the cube root of the mass-number ratio.
steps.why: R₀ is the same for both nuclei, so it divides out and the ratio of radii depends on nothing but the two mass numbers.
common_mistakes: Leaving R₀ in the answer. It cancels.
Writing (A₁/A₂)³ instead of the cube root.

recall.must_convey: That the ratio of the radii is the cube root of the ratio of the mass numbers, because R₀ cancels.
accept: cube root of A one by A two
A one by A two to the power one third
reject: R equals R nought cube root A

steps.memory_tip: The constant cancels; only the two mass numbers survive, under a cube root.

insider_note: Write R = R₀∛A first. Almost every mark lost here comes from cubing instead of taking the cube root.
